title: example
text: Suppose ’ve just installed meteobr ’s interest deal data humidity radiation june-2003 & august-2005. already checked vignette data trivia know columns ’re interested humidity radiation. first step download treated data. Unfortunately can’t large data sets easily available (data/ folder). solution let user download data ‘à la carte’; done function set_data_locally(). Even though just want analyse years 2003-2005, recommend download available data. ’s better makes easier run future analysis without wait internet connection. Note data less 900 Mb. Besides , running default set_data_locally() right away let know error data download/storage process. Talking , ’s worth mentioning following: download data . first line actually download data, second line simply note data already . shouldn’t modify .Rdata files hand. , ’s likely data downloaded , program overwrite . ’re problem process, can verify data stored ’s supposed - function local_data(). returns folder (machine) data stored. can ‘set data locally’ downloading everything GitHub data repo copying local_data() folder. function set_data_locally() called function get_data() (’ll talk next), ’s perfectly possible use package without call set_data_locally().
code: # The code bellow downloads only the data between 2003 & 2005 set_data_locally(2003:2005)  # The code bellow downloads all data available set_data_locally() year = 2010  # 1 set_data_locally(year)  # 2 set_data_locally(year) local_data()

title: example
text: Now data readily available, let’s get ! Well, us, function get_data(). first.day & last.day must format yyyy-mm-dd, columns want vars , want data across stations, stations set NULL (case, need even pass argument). Ta-dah!
code: df = get_data(first.day = "2003-06-01",               last.day  = "2005-08-31",               vars = c("humidity", "radiation"),               stations = NULL)  dplyr::glimpse(df)

title: example
text: Let’s say need data wider format. Since isn’t possible two variables (?), lets get another data. Let’s say ’re interested maximum temperature 10 11 hours UTC. code filters turn data wider format.
code: library(tidyverse) library(lubridate) library(purrr)  df_long = get_data(first.day = "2003-01-01",                    last.day  = "2003-01-31",                    vars = "temperature_max") %>%   mutate(hour = sapply(time, function(x) {x |> strsplit(" ") |> pluck(1) |> pluck(2) |> as.numeric()} )) %>%   filter(hour == 10) %>%   select(!hour)    glimpse(df_long)  df_wide = df_long %>%   mutate(time = as_factor(time)) %>%   pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = temperature_max) %>%   as_tibble()  head(df_wide)

title: example
text: everything goes wrong retire can still use get_inmet_data_by_year() rbind() data sets. downside approach function downloads processes original raw data every time ’s called, time consuming. Bellow way get data , new approach.
code: vars = c("humidity", "radiation")  df2003 = get_inmet_data_by_year(2003, first.day = "06-01", last.day = "12-31", vars = vars) df2004 = get_inmet_data_by_year(2004, vars = vars) df2005 = get_inmet_data_by_year(2005, first.day = "01-01", last.day = "08-31", vars = vars)  df = rbind(df2003, df2004, df2005) glimpse(df)
